source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Science of Plants: Botany
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: The branch of biology that deals exclusively with plants is called
questions.explanation: Botany (plant science) studies structure, function, diversity and uses of plants.

questions.stem: Historia Plantarum, an early systematic account of plants, was written by
questions.explanation: Theophrastus, a student of Aristotle, wrote Historia Plantarum and is called the Father of Botany.

questions.stem: Palynology is the botanical study of
questions.explanation: Palynology deals with pollen grains and spores, living or fossil.

questions.stem: The applied branch concerned with garden crops, ornamentals and fruit plants is
questions.explanation: Horticulture is applied botany of vegetables, fruits, flowers and landscape plants.

questions.stem: The study of fossil plants is known as
questions.explanation: Palaeobotany reconstructs extinct plants from fossils and traces plant evolution.

questions.stem: A typical plant cell wall is chemically rich in
questions.explanation: Green-plant walls are cellulose-based; chitin is fungal and peptidoglycan is bacterial.

questions.stem: Plants are the primary source of atmospheric oxygen mainly because they
questions.explanation: Oxygen released in photosynthesis is the chief biological source of O2 in air.

questions.stem: Pharmacognosy is the study of
questions.explanation: Pharmacognosy examines medicinal plants and natural crude drugs.

questions.stem: Phytogeography deals with the
questions.explanation: It maps how plant taxa are distributed across the earth’s regions.

questions.stem: A phylogenetic system of classification is based mainly on
options: economic use of the plant only
the year the plant was discovered
questions.explanation: Phylogenetic (cladistic) systems group plants by common ancestry, not one artificial trait.

questions.stem: The science of plant cells, including their organelles, is called
questions.explanation: Cytology (cell biology) studies cell structure and function; it is a pure branch of botany.

questions.stem: Birbal Sahni is especially remembered in India for work in
questions.explanation: Sahni pioneered Indian palaeobotany; the Lucknow institute of palaeobotany bears his name.

questions.stem: An artificial system of classification typically uses
options: one or a few convenient characters, ignoring phylogeny
only DNA sequences from every gene
questions.explanation: Linnaeus-style artificial keys pick a few easy traits; natural and phylogenetic systems use many characters and ancestry.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the scope of botany?
options: It includes form, function, classification and uses of plants
It studies only animals and protozoa
It is limited to naming rocks
It excludes any applied use of plants
questions.explanation: Botany covers structure, physiology, diversity, ecology and economic uses of plants.

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrectly paired?
questions.explanation: On the Origin of Species is Darwin’s; Theophrastus authored Historia Plantarum / Enquiry into Plants.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a purely descriptive (pure) branch of botany?
questions.explanation: Forestry is applied management of forests; morphology, anatomy and embryology are core pure branches.

questions.stem: Improvement of crop plants by breeding is an aspect of
questions.explanation: Plant breeding and agriculture are applied uses of botanical knowledge.

questions.stem: Which statement about palaeobotany is incorrect?
options: It is useful in tracing plant evolution
It deals only with living crop varieties
questions.explanation: Palaeobotany is about extinct/fossil plants, not modern cultivar lists.

questions.stem: Which feature is not a general diagnostic character of green plants?
questions.explanation: Chitin walls characterise fungi; green plants have cellulose walls and chloroplasts.

questions.stem: Which human need is not directly supplied by plants in the usual textbook list?
questions.explanation: Food, fibre, wood, drugs and coal/petroleum precursors come from plants; magmatic ores do not.

questions.stem: Ethnobotany is best defined as the study of
options: traditional human uses of plants in a culture
only the chromosome number of crops
questions.explanation: Ethnobotany records how communities name, grow and use plants, especially as food and medicine.

questions.stem: Plant ecology, as a branch of botany, mainly studies
options: interactions of plants with their environment
only the chemistry of a single enzyme
only the grafting of fruit trees
questions.explanation: Ecology of plants covers populations, communities and abiotic factors that shape vegetation.

questions.stem: A natural system of classification differs from an artificial system because it uses
options: a single easily seen trait only
only the economic value of the plant
questions.explanation: Natural systems (e.g. Bentham and Hooker) weigh many morphological affinities, not one arbitrary key character.

questions.stem: Which pair of branch and object of study is correct?
options: Anatomy — internal tissues of the plant body
questions.explanation: Anatomy is internal structure; palynology is pollen/spores; cytology is the cell; morphology is external form.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an applied botanical discipline?
questions.explanation: Agriculture applies plant science to food production; the other three are core pure branches.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect statement about systems of plant classification.
options: Artificial systems may use one or few convenient characters
Natural systems use many morphological affinities
Phylogenetic systems aim to reflect evolutionary history
A phylogenetic system ignores all characters except flower colour
questions.explanation: Phylogenetic systems integrate many characters (and now molecules) to recover ancestry, not a single colour trait.
